event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing, made almost exactly three years after the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic, shows that CCI still attributes tangible, present-day operational and cost pressures to the pandemic. The disclosures focus on two main vectors: (1) a persistently tight labour market with elevated turnover directly “stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic,” which is driving higher compensation and hiring costs; and (2) a rebound in travel and facilities expenses as the company transitions from pandemic-era remote work back to a hybrid/office setting. These statements are recent, explicit and describe realised cost increases rather than merely hypothetical future risks, placing them high on the severity scale under the Time Decay Principle (the event lies within the 0-3-year window). At the same time, the impacts are limited to cost inflation and workforce management rather than core revenue loss or large-scale supply chain collapse, keeping the overall risk below the maximum. Consequently, the pandemic is assessed as a meaningful, ongoing operational and cost risk with high relevance but not an existential threat.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced an extremely competitive labor market that continues to tighten due to macroeconomic conditions and elevated levels of turnover stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Direct causal link to COVID-19 pandemic is explicitly stated (“stemming from the COVID-19 pandemic”).
Describes the condition as ongoing and worsening (“continues to tighten”), signalling current and forward-looking risk.
Highlights elevated turnover and labour shortages, which can disrupt operations.
Implies higher costs to recruit and retain staff, a direct financial impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recent, explicit linkage to COVID-19 with ongoing labour-market strain and cost pressure warrants a high score of 9.

evidence_list.snippet: The increase in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily related to the growth in our business and certain costs, including travel and facilities, returning to their pre-COVID-19 pandemic levels following our return to office in February 2022.

components.reason: Explicit reference to COVID-19 pandemic establishes relevance.
Acknowledges an actual cost increase tied to pandemic-driven operational shifts (return-to-office).
Describes realised financial impact on SG&A, although not quantified.
Costs are framed as a reversion to normal levels, suggesting some stabilisation (mitigating).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete but modest evidence of pandemic-related cost rebound; impact is historical and partially normalising, so the score is moderate at 4.
